title: Closure for the repeated-scalar product differential
statement: Let $A$ be an abelian category [def-sp-abelian] with countable products [def-weil-category-product]. Assume that for every epimorphism $f:M\to N$, the product $\prod_{n\in\mathbb N}f$ is an epimorphism. Let $a:\operatorname{Id}_A\to\operatorname{Id}_A$ be natural. Put $P(M)=\prod_{n\in\mathbb N}M$ and let $s_M:P(M)\to P(M)$ have nth coordinate $a_M\circ\operatorname{pr}_{n+1}$. Put $d_M=1-s_M$. For any morphism $g:M\to N$ with $d_M,d_N$ invertible, $d_{\ker g},d_{\operatorname{coker}g},d_{\operatorname{im}g}$ are invertible. If $0\to M\to E\to N\to0$ is short exact and $d_M,d_N$ are invertible, then $d_E$ is invertible.

proof.text: The countable power functor is constant-diagram formation followed by limit. It preserves finite limits and is additive. The hypothesis says it preserves epimorphisms. Mathlib Functor.preservesHomology_of_preservesEpis_and_kernels and preservesFiniteColimits_of_preservesHomology therefore make it exact.
The coordinate formula for s is natural because a is natural; hence d is a natural endomorphism of countable power. Apply [lem-sfb-exact-endomorphism-iso-closure].

theorem iso_closure (a : 𝟭 A ⟶ 𝟭 A)
    (hE : ∀ (M N : A) (f : M ⟶ N), Epi f →
      Epi (Limits.Pi.map (fun _ : ℕ ↦ f))) :
    (∀ (M N : A) (g : M ⟶ N), IsIso ((difference a).app M) →
      IsIso ((difference a).app N) → IsIso ((difference a).app (kernel g)) ∧
      IsIso ((difference a).app (cokernel g)) ∧ IsIso ((difference a).app (image g))) ∧
    (∀ S : ShortComplex A, S.ShortExact → IsIso ((difference a).app S.X₁) →
      IsIso ((difference a).app S.X₃) → IsIso ((difference a).app S.X₂))
